clue.text: Having to maintain this source of electricity may be something of a blow

definitions.text: Having to maintain this source of electricity may be something of a blow

parts.words: Having to maintain this source of electricity may be something of a blow
parts.note: a blow is both a setback and a gust; a power source run on gusts of air is literally something of a blow

explanation.surface: A grumble that the upkeep of a power plant is a nasty setback.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind farm is a group of turbines generating electricity from moving air, a gust being a blow.

clue.text: City, was undeveloped, getting built up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, built up means written from the bottom upwards, so the run of letters is reversed

parts.note: raw means crude or undeveloped

explanation.surface: A town that was once unformed is being constructed.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator turns the whole phrase WAS RAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital city of Poland.

clue.text: Raised weapon to obtain quantity of gold?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted upwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
to get is to obtain

explanation.surface: A gun is held up to seize some gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a lump of gold found in the earth.

clue.text: Tree's condition round top of roots: excellent

parts.note: a fir is a tree

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece goes about the other

parts.note: state means condition

indicators.note: in a down clue, top of points at the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tree's health is judged by its uppermost roots, and it is splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate means of the highest quality, excellent.

clue.text: 4. say farewell on time, within limit

indicators.note: within means inside, so the farewell and the time go into the limit

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance, a limit
adios is Spanish for goodbye, a farewell

explanation.surface: Someone says goodbye punctually, within an allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: '4, say' means Radio 4, the BBC speech network, as an example; the comma is lost in the print.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio 4 is an example of a radio station, a broadcaster of radio programmes.

clue.text: Figures encapsulating University's position

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: figures, as in statistics, are stats
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Statistics are being used to describe a university's standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's position or standing relative to others, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Locate a description of some elements?

definitions.meaning: ... elements are chemical elements needed in tiny amounts

explanation.surface: Finding a description of certain chemical elements.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace is to locate, and trace elements are those occurring in minute quantities.

clue.text: It creates a stir as top one is dislodged

indicators.note: dislodged means knocked out of place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Commotion follows the removal of a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaspoon stirs tea, so it literally creates a stir.

clue.text: One's depressed to find another case

definitions.text: One's depressed to find another case

parts.words: One's depressed to find another case
parts.note: a keyboard key pressed down to switch letters to upper case, read as someone gloomy at a fresh problem

explanation.surface: A detective sinks into gloom on discovering yet another case.
explanation.definitionFit: The shift key is held down to type capital letters, the other case.

clue.text: Anger about customary view of fashion business

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: anger is rage
trad, short for traditional, describes the customary way of seeing things

explanation.surface: Someone fumes at the conventional outlook of the clothing industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trad' is an informal word for traditional, as in trad jazz, so it stands for the customary outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: The rag trade is an informal term for the clothing and fashion industry.

clue.text: I'm taken aback about a ruling in African country

indicators.note: about means surrounding the following pieces
taken aback read literally means turned to face backwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: I'm written without its apostrophe gives these two letters
a ruling, a law, is a rule laid down

explanation.surface: A traveller is startled by a regulation in an African state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' turns IM into MI, which goes about A plus LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked country in south-east Africa.

clue.text: Violent storms, any one that could do for building work

indicators.note: violent suggests things being thrown about, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Fierce gales might wreck any construction.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonemasonry is the craft of building with cut stone.

clue.text: Spy's information coming in late, after extremists are eradicated

indicators.note: coming in signals that one piece enters another
removing the extremes, the first and last letters, of the word late leaves its middle

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A spy's intelligence arrives too late, once the radicals have been wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after extremists are eradicated' strips the first and last letters from 'late', leaving AT; 'gen' is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is a secret operative, a spy working for an intelligence service.

clue.text: In a difficult position replacing ball from pocket here?

definitions.meaning: put under pressure to act or answer immediately
in snooker a potted coloured ball is put back on its marked place on the table

explanation.surface: A snooker player is in trouble while putting a potted ball back.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both under pressure and, literally, on the marked place where snooker balls are respotted.

clue.text: How one trifles with some diet — and what clothes subsequently become?

parts.note: a fast is a kind of diet, eating nothing
after dieting, clothes become baggy or loose

explanation.surface: A dieter toys with eating less and finds clothes hang baggier afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To play fast and loose is to trifle irresponsibly, so the phrase describes how one trifles.

clue.text: After working all morning one gets to stuff around now

definitions.text: After working all morning one gets to stuff around now

parts.words: After working all morning one gets to stuff around now
parts.note: after a morning's work one may eat one's fill at this point in the day

explanation.surface: A worker is ready to gorge after a long morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunchtime is the middle of the day when people eat after the morning's work.

clue.text: Incredibly OK. or the reverse of OK?

definitions.meaning: KO, the letters OK reversed, is short for this boxing term

explanation.surface: Something is either astonishingly fine or the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockout is a stunner, and KO, OK backwards, abbreviates a knockout in boxing.

clue.text: Society's expression of grief is all-encompassing

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society
weeping expresses grief

explanation.surface: A community's mourning is total.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping means wide-ranging, covering everything.

clue.text: Will's later amendment part of desert island bookshelf?

definitions.meaning: a newer version of a will, a will being a testament
castaways on the radio show Desert Island Discs are given the Bible, of which this is a part

explanation.surface: A revised will and a holiday reading list seem to be discussed.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert Island Discs is a long-running BBC radio programme in which each guest is given the Bible and Shakespeare to take to the island.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament is the second part of the Bible, and literally a new testament, a later will.

clue.text: Pacific island-one that enthralls one in reflection

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: enthralls means holds captive, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Pacific island captivates someone lost in thought.
explanation.walkthrough: I plus THAT holding I gives ITIHAT; 'in reflection' turns the whole run.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Nick article? That's five inside

indicators.note: inside means within, so these letters go into the article

parts.note: the is the definite article
i.e., id est, means that is
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A question about whether an item is the fifth one.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick is British slang for steal, which is to thieve.

clue.text: Warring countries may be stupid

indicators.note: warring suggests conflict and disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Nations at war may be acting foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cretinous is an offensive word meaning very stupid.

clue.text: In finer type, it's readable still

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the answer lies inside these words

explanation.surface: Small print is said to remain legible.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless, still.

clue.text: King abandoning domestic area — for this blasted place?

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving out, so the letter goes from the word

parts.note: the hearth is the fireside, the heart of the home
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch leaves the fireside for a wild, storm-struck spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'blasted heath' is where Macbeth meets the witches in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: A heath is open, wild land, famously the blasted one of Macbeth.

clue.text: Actor spurning one Dickensian role?

indicators.note: spurning means rejecting, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: Laurence Olivier, the great English actor
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A star turns down a part in an adaptation of Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is the title character of the Dickens novel, a role in stage and screen versions.

clue.text: I note penalty, after receiving it, as incredibly large

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a fine is a penalty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notices a fine and, once handed it, finds it enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinite means without limit, which is beyond large, so incredibly large is a fair hyperbole.

clue.text: Drunk beginning to struggle with elasticated clothing

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk

indicators.note: beginning to points at the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A tipsy person wrestles with stretchy garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights are close-fitting stretchy legwear.

clue.text: This is SE? Deny it furiously!

definitions.text: This is SE? Deny it furiously!

indicators.note: furiously suggests wild agitation, so these letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: the letters as written, standing for south-east

explanation.surface: An indignant northerner rejects the claim that their region is in the south-east.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside, around Newcastle, is in the north-east of England, so anyone there would furiously deny being SE.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the region: a place whose people would angrily deny being in the south-east.
